doFirst.why: He is 79.4% rostered across ESPN and sitting as a free agent here, so he costs you nothing — and that matters more in this league than in Chem, because a waiver claim would drop you to last for the entire season and never reset. You dropped Meyers on the 9th to add Boutte; the reporting has moved since, and this is the same transaction back the other way at zero cost. He does not start this week — Golden projects ahead of him and the flex is spoken for — so take him as the floor piece behind Wilson and Rice, not as an upgrade you play today.

action.label: Add Jakobi Meyers, drop Kayshon Boutte

trades.headline: Their second quarterback scores them nothing every week and their RB2 is Rachaad White
trades.yourSurplus: Lloyd is your fourth running back behind Taylor, Barkley and Tuten, and he is the one asset here where ESPN and the consensus point opposite ways. ESPN has Lloyd 12.8 to Tuten's 12.0; the consensus has Tuten RB25 and Lloyd RB33. Believe the consensus: PFN gives Lloyd 14-17 carries but says plainly there is no evidence he can withstand an NFL beating, on one career game and a lost 2025, while Tuten is the lead back on a team favoured by 9.5 with the highest implied total of anyone you own. So Tuten keeps the flex and Lloyd is the piece to move — you are selling the back ESPN prices high and the market prices low.
trades.theirHole: Team 13 starts Josh Allen and benches Lamar Jackson in a one-quarterback league, so one of the two best quarterbacks in football scores them zero all season. Meanwhile their starting RB2 is Rachaad White at 8.9 and their bench answer is Blake Corum at 9.4.
trades.yourLineup: Your quarterback becomes Lamar (18.1, QB rank 2) instead of the Stafford/Lawrence committee that has been projecting about 16. Tuten stays in the flex, so the only thing you actually give up is your RB4.
trades.theirLineup: Lloyd walks into their RB2 slot as Green Bay's listed starter with Jacobs barred for the season, worth about +3.4 to their best lineup, and costs them a quarterback they can never play.
trades.risk: Lloyd is the one piece here with real upside — if he holds the Green Bay job with Jacobs on the exempt list all year, he could out-earn a quarterback upgrade in full PPR. You are selling the volatile asset and buying the certain one. Also note the honest limitation: only weekly projections are published, so both gains above are one-week numbers and season-long value is the right unit for a trade. The season-long case is stronger than +0.7 suggests, because it also lets you drop a quarterback.

candidates.note: Ignore the rank. Travis Hunter carries an analyst-consensus rank of 1 in this file against a 5.6 projection, and the projection is the one telling the truth: Jacksonville lists him as a starting cornerback and a backup receiver behind Parker Washington, Brian Thomas Jr. and Jakobi Meyers. Liam Coen has described a steady increase in his defensive work, and the staff would rather he take mental reps on the sideline than play offence — he ran 67% of offensive snaps in 2025 and will not come close to that now. Maye-day dropping him on the 9th was correct, not a blunder, and he is 65.8% rostered here because the rest of the league has not looked past the label. This row exists so you do not spend a roster spot on it.

Chris Rodriguez Jr. is the reason your flex starter's projection is soft — he is Jacksonville's goal-line back and the specific worry analysts name against Tuten's touch count. At 31.1% rostered he is a handcuff to the player you are starting today and a free agent, so he costs no waiver priority in a league where priority never resets. Marginal while your roster is full; the name to reach for if Tuten's touches go the wrong way.
